meta.name: Carrot Cake with Brown Butter Cream Cheese Frosting
meta.description: A research-backed carrot cake synthesized from 64 sources — Michelin-star chefs, JBF award winners, food science, and competition bake-off data. Oil-based for moisture, with spices bloomed in warm oil for amplified flavor. Finished with a brown butter cream cheese frosting using Nancy Silverton's cold-cream-cheese technique. Designed for exceptional results with one-bowl simplicity.

change_log.summary: Initial recipe synthesized from 9-agent research across 64 sources (Michelin/JBF chefs, food science, competition winners, community intel)

vessels.name: Large Mixing Bowl
vessels.reuse: Wet mix → fold batter → empty into pans → clean → beat frosting

vessels.name: Light-Colored Saucepan
vessels.reuse: Bloom spices in oil → clean → brown butter

vessels.name: Medium Bowl
vessels.reuse: Dry ingredients → freed → catch brown butter for chilling

ingredients.name: All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 9/9 agents — universal for carrot cake. AP, not cake flour (too weak for heavy batter with mix-ins)
ingredients.rationale: Every source surveyed uses all-purpose flour. Cake flour produces too delicate a crumb for the weight of carrots and nuts.

ingredients.name: Baking Powder
ingredients.rationale: Provides the main rise. Used alongside baking soda for insurance — dual leavening is universal in acclaimed recipes.

ingredients.name: Baking Soda
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 9/9 agents — ATK food science confirms it softens carrots and promotes browning
ingredients.rationale: Softens carrot fibers during baking (ATK), promotes Maillard browning, and activates with the acid in brown sugar.

ingredients.name: Ground Cinnamon
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 9/9 agents — the defining spice, present in every recipe surveyed
ingredients.rationale: Universal. Bloom in warm oil for up to 10x flavor amplification (ATK/MasalaBear food science).

ingredients.name: Ground Ginger
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 2: 6/9 agents — third most common spice after cinnamon and nutmeg
ingredients.rationale: Warm, peppery heat complements cinnamon. Bloom with other spices in oil.

ingredients.name: Ground Nutmeg
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 2: 6/9 agents — second most common spice after cinnamon
ingredients.rationale: Warm, slightly sweet. Small amount adds complexity without being identifiable. Bloom in oil.

ingredients.name: Ground Cloves
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 3: 4/9 agents — potent, easy to overpower
ingredients.rationale: Extremely potent — a pinch adds warmth and depth. Bloom in oil with other spices.

ingredients.name: Fine Salt
ingredients.rationale: Balances sweetness in both cake and frosting.

ingredients.name: Canola Oil
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 9/9 agents — oil stays liquid when cold, coats gluten, more forgiving than butter
ingredients.rationale: Oil-based cake is the universal consensus. Stays moist even when cold (butter solidifies). Also serves as the blooming medium for spices.

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 9/9 agents — roughly 50/50 split with brown sugar, ~300-400g total
ingredients.rationale: Provides clean sweetness and structure. Split with brown sugar for depth.

ingredients.name: Dark Brown Sugar (packed)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 9/9 agents — molasses depth, moisture, acid for baking soda
ingredients.rationale: Adds moisture, molasses flavor, and provides acid to activate baking soda.

ingredients.name: Large Eggs (room temp)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 9/9 agents — near-universal at 4 large eggs
ingredients.rationale: Structure, moisture, and emulsification. Room temperature for better incorporation into oil-based batter.

ingredients.name: Vanilla Extract
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 2: 6/9 agents — in cake and/or frosting
ingredients.rationale: Rounds out spice flavor in cake, adds warmth to frosting.

ingredients.name: Orange Zest
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 2: 5/9 agents — brightens heavy spice, natural pairing with carrot
ingredients.rationale: Citrus brightness cuts through the richness. A small amount lifts the entire flavor profile.

ingredients.name: Fresh Carrots (fine-grated)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 9/9 agents — NEVER pre-shredded. Small holes of box grater for max moisture and even distribution
ingredients.rationale: The defining ingredient. Fine-grate on the small holes of a box grater — smaller shreds distribute more evenly and release more moisture into the batter.

ingredients.name: Pecans
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 8/9 agents — always toasted. Pecans = sweeter/buttery vs walnuts = earthier
ingredients.rationale: Toast before adding for maximum flavor and to reduce sogginess in batter. Pecans chosen over walnuts for their buttery sweetness.

ingredients.name: Unsalted Butter
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 2: 6/9 agents — brown butter frosting is the #1 elevation move (Silverton, Parks, Saffitz)
ingredients.rationale: All butter goes to the frosting. Browned for nutty, caramel depth — independently endorsed by Silverton, Parks, Saffitz, and The Kitchn bake-off winner.

ingredients.name: Cream Cheese (full-fat, block)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 9/9 agents — cream cheese frosting is the only frosting for carrot cake
ingredients.rationale: Must be cold from fridge (Silverton technique) for stable frosting. Block-style, not spreadable.

ingredients.name: Powdered Sugar
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Frosting consensus — sift before adding to prevent lumps
ingredients.rationale: Sweetens and stabilizes the frosting. Sifting is essential for smooth texture.

states.title: Preheat Oven
states.direction: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat to 350°F (175°C).
states.exit_condition: Oven preheating

states.title: Prepare Cake Pans
states.direction: Grease two 23cm (9") round cake pans with butter or nonstick spray. Line bottoms with parchment rounds.
states.exit_condition: Both pans greased and lined with parchment

notes.text: Trace the pan on parchment, cut just inside the line for a clean fit

states.title: Brown the Butter
states.direction: Cut 226g unsalted butter into tablespoon-sized pieces. Melt in a light-colored saucepan over medium heat, swirling occasionally. Cook until milk solids turn deep golden brown and butter smells nutty.
states.exit_condition: Milk solids are coffee-colored, butter smells toasty and nutty

notes.text: Use a light-colored pan so you can see the milk solids browning
Watch carefully past 5 minutes — goes from brown to burnt in seconds

states.title: Cool Brown Butter
states.direction: Immediately transfer browned butter to medium bowl. Stir in 4g vanilla extract. Let cool to room temperature.
states.exit_condition: Brown butter at room temperature, vanilla mixed in

states.title: Chill Brown Butter
states.direction: Cover bowl and refrigerate until completely solid.
states.exit_condition: Brown butter is completely solid — can be cut into cubes

notes.text: Can be done overnight — even better for flavor development
While butter chills, proceed to toast nuts and make the cake

states.title: Toast Pecans
states.direction: Spread 115g pecans on rimmed sheet pan in a single layer. Toast at 350°F (175°C) for 8 minutes until fragrant and slightly darkened.
states.exit_condition: Pecans fragrant, slightly darkened, oil visible on surface

notes.text: Toasting is critical — develops flavor and prevents sogginess in batter

states.title: Cool & Chop Pecans
states.direction: Transfer toasted pecans to cutting board. Cool briefly, then roughly chop.
states.exit_condition: Pecans roughly chopped and cooled enough to handle

states.title: Bloom Spices in Oil
states.direction: Warm 240g canola oil gently in saucepan over medium-low heat. Add cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves. Stir constantly for 15 seconds until fragrant. Remove from heat immediately.
states.exit_condition: Oil is fragrant with bloomed spices, removed from heat

notes.text: Do NOT overheat — spices burn quickly. Oil should be warm, not smoking
Blooming extracts fat-soluble flavor compounds, amplifying spice intensity up to 10x (ATK/MasalaBear)

states.title: Cool Spiced Oil
states.direction: Let spiced oil cool to room temperature before mixing with other ingredients.
states.exit_condition: Spiced oil warm but not hot to the touch

notes.text: Hot oil will scramble the eggs — wait until comfortable to touch the outside of the pan

states.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
states.direction: In large mixing bowl, whisk together cooled spiced oil, granulated sugar, brown sugar, eggs, vanilla extract, and orange zest until smooth and glossy.
states.exit_condition: Mixture is smooth, glossy, and well combined

states.title: Combine Dry Ingredients
states.direction: In medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
states.exit_condition: Dry ingredients evenly whisked, no clumps

states.title: Fold Dry into Wet
states.direction: Add dry ingredients to wet mixture. Fold with rubber spatula until just combined — some small streaks of flour are OK.
states.exit_condition: No large flour pockets, batter is thick and slightly lumpy

notes.text: Do NOT overmix — develops gluten and makes cake tough

states.title: Fold in Carrots & Pecans
states.direction: Fold in freshly grated carrots and chopped toasted pecans until evenly distributed.
states.exit_condition: Carrots and pecans evenly distributed through batter

notes.text: Grate carrots on the small holes of a box grater — not large shreds
Batter will be very thick and heavy — this is correct

states.title: Fill Pans
states.direction: Divide batter evenly between the two prepared 23cm (9") round pans. Level tops gently with an offset spatula.
states.exit_condition: Batter divided evenly between pans, tops smoothed

notes.text: Weigh pans on the kitchen scale to ensure even layers

states.title: Bake
states.direction: Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 35-40 minutes, rotating pans 180° halfway through.
states.exit_condition: Internal temperature 205°F (96°C), or cake springs back when gently pressed

notes.text: Internal thermometer is more reliable than toothpick for dense cakes with mix-ins
Rotate pans at the halfway mark for even browning

states.title: Cool in Pans
states.direction: Set pans on wire cooling rack. Cool for 15 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Cakes pulled slightly from edges, pans cool enough to handle

states.title: Unmold Cakes
states.direction: Run a thin knife around pan edges. Invert onto wire cooling rack. Peel off parchment. Flip cakes right-side up.
states.exit_condition: Both cake layers on wire rack, parchment removed

states.title: Cool Completely
states.direction: Cool cake layers completely on wire rack before frosting.
states.exit_condition: Cake layers completely cool to touch — no warmth at center

notes.text: Frosting warm cake will melt the cream cheese frosting
For best results, wrap cooled layers in plastic and refrigerate overnight — next-day cake is even better

states.title: Cube the Brown Butter
states.direction: Remove solid brown butter from fridge. Cut into 1cm cubes.
states.exit_condition: Brown butter cubed and ready to beat

notes.text: If butter is too hard to cut, let it sit at room temp for 5 minutes

states.title: Beat Brown Butter
states.direction: In large mixing bowl (or stand mixer with paddle), beat brown butter cubes on medium speed until smooth and creamy.
states.exit_condition: Brown butter is smooth, light, and creamy

states.title: Add Cream Cheese
states.direction: Cut cold cream cheese into cubes. Add to brown butter. Mix on medium speed until combined and glossy.
states.exit_condition: Mixture is smooth, glossy, and combined

notes.text: Cream cheese MUST be cold from the fridge — room temp cream cheese makes runny frosting
Do not overbeat or frosting will thin out

states.title: Add Sugar & Salt
states.direction: Reduce mixer speed to low. Add sifted powdered sugar and salt. Mix until just smooth.
states.exit_condition: Frosting is smooth, thick, and spreadable

notes.text: Sift powdered sugar first to prevent lumps

states.title: Frost First Layer
states.direction: Place first cake layer on serving plate or cake board. Spread approximately one-third of frosting evenly over the top.
states.exit_condition: First layer has an even coat of frosting

notes.text: Tuck strips of parchment under the edges to keep the plate clean while frosting

states.title: Frost Top & Sides
states.direction: Place second cake layer on top, pressing gently to level. Spread remaining frosting over top and sides.
states.exit_condition: Cake fully frosted — top and sides covered

states.title: Chill to Set
states.direction: Refrigerate assembled cake for at least 30 minutes to set the frosting before slicing.
states.exit_condition: Frosting is firm to touch, cake holds shape when sliced

notes.text: Store leftovers covered in refrigerator for up to 5 days
Let slices sit at room temp 10-15 minutes before serving for best texture

research.strategy: 9 parallel search agents across distinct strategies: Michelin/fine dining chef recipes, competition bake-off winners, critically acclaimed pattern analysis (15 recipes), food science (oil vs butter, spice blooming, leavening), practical consistency (one-bowl methods), cleanup efficiency (vessel minimization), community intel (Reddit, forums), add-ins debate (raisins/pineapple/coconut), and frosting mastery (brown butter technique). Cross-referenced ingredient confidence across all agents. Most similar existing recipe: King Arthur's Carrot Cake (won 2 independent bake-offs), with two key upgrades — bloomed spices and brown butter frosting.

techniques.name: Spice Blooming in Oil
techniques.rationale: Warming ground spices in oil for 10-15 seconds extracts fat-soluble flavor compounds, amplifying spice intensity up to 10x compared to dry mixing into batter.

techniques.name: Brown Butter Cream Cheese Frosting (Silverton Technique)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Nancy Silverton, Stella Parks, Claire Saffitz
techniques.rationale: Browning butter creates nutty caramel depth. Silverton's key insight: solidify brown butter, cube, then beat with cold cream cheese for a stable, flavorful frosting that won't thin out.

techniques.name: Fine-Grate Carrots (Small Holes)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Universal — 9/9 agents, Food Republic technique guide
techniques.rationale: Small holes of a box grater produce finer shreds that distribute more evenly and release more moisture into the batter. Never use pre-shredded carrots.

techniques.name: Dual Leavening (Baking Soda + Baking Powder)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Universal — 9/9 agents, American Society of Baking
techniques.rationale: Baking soda softens carrot fibers and promotes Maillard browning; baking powder provides primary lift. Both together ensure consistent rise in a dense, heavy batter.

techniques.name: Internal Temperature for Doneness (205°F / 96°C)
techniques.rationale: More reliable than toothpick test for dense cakes with mix-ins that can fool visual checks. Insert thermometer into the center of the cake.

techniques.name: Oil-Based (Not Butter) for Moisture
techniques.rationale: Oil stays liquid when cold (butter solidifies), producing a cake that is moist even straight from the fridge. Also simpler to mix — no creaming step needed.
